en.headline: Labour chief says humans remain masters in AI-driven workplace
en.dek: Chris Sun told a university summit that demand for AI practitioners combining technical and domain skills would rise three- to fourfold, rejecting zero-sum replacement fears.
body: Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun said on Wednesday that the future of work lay in human-machine collaboration rather than machines replacing people, with humans remaining the masters.

Speaking at the Global University Presidents and Leaders Summit, Sun said employers sought staff who paired AI know-how with deep domain expertise and strong soft skills. He predicted demand for such AI practitioners would grow three- to fourfold, from around 4,500 to 20,000 in the coming years.

Sun rejected the idea that automation represented a zero-sum game that would simply destroy jobs, saying AI was destroying some roles while creating others. He emphasised a shift in mindset toward partnerships that create value.

zh.headline: 勞福局局長：人工智能時代人機協作 人類仍是主導
zh.dek: 孫玉薚在大學峰會指，結合技術與專業知識的人工智能從業者需求將增三至四倍，並否定零和取代論。
body: 勞工及福利局局長孫玉薚周三表示，未來職場在於人機協作，而非機器取代人類，人類仍是主導者。
他在全球大學校長及領袖峰會上說，僱主希望員工同時具備人工智能知識、深厚專業範疇專長及良好軟技能。他預測這類人工智能從業者的需求將由約4500人增至20000人，增幅達三至四倍。
孫玉薚指出，人工智能會淘汰部分職位同時創造新職位，並非零和遊戲。他強調需改變思維，透過人機合作創造價值。
